chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Why Hinton calls him a super sideman: knowing everybody's part
summary: Jackson argues hearing and remembering notes is simple, and says in Ellington's band he knew the saxophone parts and filled in on bass.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: But this is one reason why you are considered of all the players really and truly a super sideman, because I can't know of anybody that had the ears to listen and the concern with the entire orchestra to listen to everybody's part and to remember it and memorize it. So they've been people -- If

somebody was late or somebody couldn't show up, you could play it on your individual instrument. You could play the other guy's part, which was absolutely amazing. I know of no other musician in all the annals of jazz -- and I don't know anything too much about the other, the classical end of it -- but I don't know of anybody I ever heard of, any musician, classical or otherwise speak of anybody that knew everybody's part. I'm sure there must be others, maybe, in other worlds but certainly not in jazz.

Well, you see, that wasn't -- to me, I don't know. I used to argue with guys about this ear thing. You know, I figure if you hear an A tomorrow, today, or you hear a B-flat or C or you hear a D and you hear the note, why, tomorrow, when you hear that note, you don't know what it is? Now, I will argue that to my dying day, because to me that's so simple. It's so simple, you know. Why you can't -- Why you don't know what these notes are when you play them every day and you hear them?

You know, in Duke's band I heard these arrangements, right? I heard everybody's part. I used to listen to the saxophone section and I knew their parts by listening to it because I was -- you know, I'd get so wrapped up
in these things and it was phenomenal. And even in Duke's band I played bass. When Wendell would be out, I could play in his place.
